transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together because I need to finalize the middle school civics assessment administration plan for our May testing window. As you may know, the draft plan currently places all registered students in a single administration in the main hall on May 14, using four general proctors. Before I can issue the final plan, our standing pre-administration routine requires me to get confirmation from each of you on your respective areas -- facilities, enrollment, staffing, and student scheduling. I'd like to go around the table and hear from each of you so we can identify any issues before I approve the plan.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a facilities issue. The main hall is reserved for a school board meeting on May 14, so it's not available for testing that day. However, the library has been cleared for state testing with 40 individual desks. I confirmed the reservation and clearance with facilities this week, but the testing calendar still lists the main hall. We'll need to update the plan to use the library instead.

Only two available staff members hold current state-testing proctor certifications, and state rules require one certified proctor and one trained monitor in each testing room. I verified the certificates against the state roster this week, but the staffing list still labels all four people only as general proctors. So we don't have enough certified proctors for the four the draft plan assumes, and we'll need to account for the certification requirement in whatever rooms we end up using.
